# Disagreement Log — Acts of Thomas, Chapter 3
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "I have found a man who is a carpenter and a builder" vs. "I have found the man you sought"
- **EMET:** "I have found a man who is a carpenter and a builder, as you commanded me"
- **LOGOS:** "I have found the man you sought — a carpenter and a builder, as you commanded me"
- **PNEUMA:** "I found what you needed — a carpenter and a builder"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "what you needed" depersonalizes Thomas. LOGOS's "the man you sought" is cleaner.

### v.2 — "What is your skill?" vs. "What can you do?"
- **EMET:** "What is your skill? Can you build me a palace?"
- **LOGOS:** "What is your skill? Can you build me a palace?"
- **PNEUMA:** "What can you do? Can you build me a palace?"
- **Note:** "What is your skill?" (EMET/LOGOS) is more formal and appropriate for a royal commission.

### v.4 — "walked for a great distance" vs. "considerable distance" vs. "a long way"
- **EMET:** "walked for a great distance"
- **LOGOS:** "walked a considerable distance"
- **PNEUMA:** "walked a long way"
- **Note:** Minor register differences. "Considerable distance" (LOGOS) is natural.

### v.5 — "I will build something great" — all agents agree.
- **PNEUMA** adds "something to behold" — minor embellishment.

### v.7 — "this is my work" vs. "this is my craft"
- **EMET:** "this is my work"
- **LOGOS:** "this is my craft"
- **PNEUMA:** implied
- **Note:** "Craft" (LOGOS) is more precise for a skilled trade. Minor.

### v.8 — "commissioned him well" vs. "made generous provision"
- **EMET:** "commissioned him well and commanded him to receive"
- **LOGOS:** "made generous provision for him, commanding"
- **PNEUMA:** "He was generous... ordered that Thomas should have access"
- **Note:** "Access to the treasury" (PNEUMA) is a paraphrase; "receive from the treasury" (LOGOS) is more precise.

### v.9 — "went about the villages and cities" vs. "went throughout"
- **EMET:** "went about the villages and cities"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "went throughout the villages and cities"
- **Note:** Minor. Equivalent.

### v.9 — "And I am indeed building him one" — all agents agree on the centrality of this statement. Minor punctuation/emphasis differences only.

### v.13 — "The palace is finished and lacks nothing but the roof" vs. "Nearly done. Finished, actually — just waiting on the roof." (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** Retain the formal statement.
- **PNEUMA:** "Nearly done... Finished, actually" — PNEUMA has Thomas contradict himself within two sentences.
- **Note:** PNEUMA's self-correction is not in source. Thomas states the palace is finished and needs only the roof — that is the complete statement.

### v.14 — "was glad" vs. "was delighted"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "was glad"
- **PNEUMA:** "was delighted"
- **Note:** Minor. "Glad" (EMET/LOGOS) is more literal; "delighted" is slightly elevated.

---
*10 disagreements. SOPHIA: "What is your skill?" (v.2); "made generous provision" (v.8); reject PNEUMA's self-contradiction in v.13; "was glad" (v.14).*
